A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research framework, renamed from TimePD to TimeID. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original forecasting comparisons, component ablations, sensitivity experiments and prediction visualizations in Section 4 and Appendix A.3.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds original baseline comparisons, dataset evaluations, sensitivity analyses, zero-shot experiments and resource measurements.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the decomposition, invariant masking, Fourier supervision, gradient alignment, proxy correction, distillation and overall objective. The renaming, additional hyperparameter disclosures and IDFL pseudocode do not establish a changed proposed method; the Chronos proxy replacement is an experimental variant.

E1.justification: v3 adds evaluations on Exchange, Solar and PEMS03 in Appendix A.2.17, extending coverage to exchange-rate forecasting and additional solar-energy and traffic data. The original seven datasets and alternative-source transfer pairs are retained.

E2.justification: The original eleven forecasting baselines remain. v3 additionally evaluates Chronos, UniTS, MOIRAI and Moment in Table 2; ADvSKM, CoDATS and SASA in Table 9; and moving-average, wavelet and Gaussian denoising alternatives in Table 5.

E3.justification: The original splits, 30% target adaptation and forecasting horizons are retained. Added evaluation designs include source-only zero-shot inference, foundation-model comparisons explicitly using lookback 336 and horizon 96, controlled proxy replacements, extensive parameter grids, and training-time/memory measurements. These broaden the protocol without establishing changes to the retained experiments.

E4.justification: v1 ablates LLM, proxy denoising and distillation and studies target-data size and learning rate. v3 additionally ablates IDFL and gradient invariance, examines five loss weights plus correction strength, masking percentile and decomposition kernel length, compares alternative denoisers and a Chronos proxy, and adds optimization and zero-shot analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations or significance tests. The added tables and plots continue reporting point estimates without statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: All 432 numerical results in Table 1 and all 72 in v1 Table 2, retained as v3 Table 4, are unchanged. v3 adds substantial new results: for example, Table 2 reports Traffic MSE of 0.368 for MOIRAI versus 0.452 for TimeID, while Table 7 reports Exchange MSE of 0.102 for TimeID versus 0.111 for PatchTST. New ablation, sensitivity, zero-shot and efficiency results further expand the evidence.

T1.justification: The forecasting, invariant-feature and proxy-confidence definitions in Appendix A.1 are retained, as are the substantive mathematical arguments. Added standard MAE/MSE formulas and derivative-notation cleanup do not introduce new theory, assumptions or proofs.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a first source-free forecasting framework combining invariant disentanglement, LLM proxy denoising and distillation. The introduction's claimed average MSE/MAE improvements of 10.7%/9.3% remain unchanged; v3 also states both figures in the abstract. Renaming and added supporting experiments do not redefine the central contribution.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive applicability boundaries: weak zero-shot performance without adaptation and foundation-model advantages on Traffic. It also explains denoising as correction of systematic forecasting shifts, interprets regularization and decomposition tradeoffs, and discusses severe negative transfer at a low masking percentile and the weaker Chronos-proxy results.

D1.justification: v3 supplies a code-repository link, separate IDFL pseudocode, previously unspecified defaults including kernel length 25, masking percentile 0.3, correction strength 1, seasonal ratio 20%, and additional loss weights. Table 3 newly reports training time, GPU memory and target-model parameter count. These are documentation additions, not evidence that retained experiments used different settings.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands references and comparative positioning around time-series foundation models and domain-adaptation methods. Whereas v1 explicitly excluded foundation-model comparisons, v3 compares against them and discusses single-source adaptation relative to broad pretraining, alongside new comparisons with ADvSKM, CoDATS and SASA.

P1.justification: v3 changes the title and framework name, rewrites the abstract and makes local wording corrections. It reorganizes experimental setup into subsections, moves dataset/baseline descriptions into the main text and relocates invariant-feature visualization to the appendix. The original introduction, methodological exposition and overall section sequence remain largely intact.

P2.justification: The document changes from a single-column to a two-column layout, extensively resizing and rearranging displays. Ablation panels are expanded and regrouped, the invariant-feature visualization is relocated, and numerous new comparison tables, sensitivity plots, a training-loss plot and an additional algorithm display materially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v3 addresses important validation gaps in v1 by directly testing the central IDFL and gradient-invariance components, adding stronger comparison families, and documenting failure conditions. Newly disclosed defaults, resource measurements and code-access information substantially improve auditability despite unchanged main benchmark scores. Some new protocols remain thinly specified, the added IDFL pseudocode has loss-notation inconsistencies, and statistical uncertainty remains absent, but the gains in component validation and applicability assessment are substantial.
